source.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks

license.changes: Cropped from the original figure. Source colors and geometry are preserved.

teaching.spokenAnchor: Domain-adaptive pretraining uses unlabeled material from the domain, such as the incident runbooks and API corpus. Task-adaptive pretraining uses the task’s own unlabeled inputs, possibly a much smaller subset. The original Don’t Stop Pretraining experiments used masked-language-model RoBERTa across domains and classification tasks.
teaching.moment: Map domain data and task data to different adaptation distributions before choosing DAPT or TAPT.
teaching.scope: The source experiments use masked RoBERTa; the figure does not promise the same gains for the decoder-only toy.
teaching.caption: Task data, target-domain data, and original pretraining data have different distributions.
